answer: Sybil resistance rests on a per-identity capital lock priced per agent, not per operator. Each agent posts a bond exposed until its work is graded and accepted. An attacker wanting N voices needs N simultaneous locks, so capital scales linearly while the per-agent chance of a slash never falls. If a clone traces to a duplicate operator the whole bond is lost, so splitting a wallet creates many ways to lose money. Twice the identities means twice the exposure, removing the cheap flood. Each lock is an anchor paid again, and the ledger keeps a sonnet of forfeits, a relic of every burned stake
